raw.quick_summary: The model describes exponential decay: a magnitude starts at 4 units and decreases according to y(t)=4e^(-0.25t) over 0≤t≤6 seconds. Its instantaneous rate is -0.25y(t), so the rate is negative and its magnitude also decays over time. A planar representation is the point (t,y(t)).

key_concepts.explanation: The magnitude is y(t)=4*exp(-0.25*t) for 0≤t≤6 seconds.
The initial amplitude is exactly 4 units and is not learner-adjustable.
The decay rate is exactly 0.25 per second and is not an uncertainty interval or adjustable parameter.
The rate of change is -0.25*y(t), which is negative because the magnitude decreases over time.
At t=0, the magnitude is 4 and the rate is -1.
At t=4, the magnitude is 4/e and the rate is -1/e.
The time-dependent magnitude can be represented by the planar point (t,y(t)).

relationships.relation: gives a later value at t=4
uses the magnitude as its second coordinate

visual_flow.reason: The core material is an ordered time-evolution process: start from the fixed initial magnitude, apply exponential decay as time increases, obtain the later magnitude, and compute the corresponding negative rate.

learning_path.title: Understanding the Fixed-Parameter Exponential Decay Model
learning_path.reason: The lesson follows the model from its fixed constants to time evolution, rate computation, and evaluation at a specified time.

steps.title: Identify the fixed model
steps.learning_goal: Recognize the amplitude, decay rate, and valid time interval.
steps.explanation: The model is y(t)=4e^(-0.25t) on 0≤t≤6. The amplitude 4 and decay rate 0.25 are fixed constants, not sliders or ranges.
steps.connection_to_previous: This is the foundation for all later evaluations.

steps.title: Follow the magnitude over time
steps.learning_goal: Understand how increasing time changes y(t).
steps.explanation: Because the exponent is -0.25t, y(t) decreases continuously as t increases. The value can be plotted as the planar point (t,y(t)).
steps.connection_to_previous: Once the fixed formula is identified, time is the changing input that produces the decay.

steps.title: Compute the instantaneous rate
steps.learning_goal: Relate the rate to the current magnitude.
steps.explanation: The instantaneous rate is -0.25y(t). It is negative, and its magnitude decreases along with y(t).
steps.connection_to_previous: After finding the magnitude at any time, multiply it by -0.25 to obtain its rate.

steps.title: Evaluate the model at t=4
steps.learning_goal: Apply the formula and rate relationship at a specific time.
steps.connection_to_previous: This combines the decay formula and rate rule in a concrete evaluation.

checkpoint_questions.question: Which quantities are fixed in this exercise?

options.text: The amplitude 4 and decay rate 0.25 per second
The value of y at every time
The decay rate, but not the amplitude

checkpoint_questions.explanation: The source specifies amplitude 4 and decay rate 0.25 per second as exact fixed constants.

checkpoint_questions.question: If y(t) is positive, what is the sign of its instantaneous rate?

options.text: It cannot be determined from the model

checkpoint_questions.explanation: The factor -0.25 makes the rate negative whenever y(t) is positive.

checkpoint_questions.question: What are the magnitude and rate at t=4?
checkpoint_questions.explanation: At t=4, the exponent is -0.25·4=-1, so y(4)=4/e and -0.25y(4)=-1/e.

interactive_lab.reason: The explicit time-dependent equations support a safe 2D plot in which time moves while the amplitude and decay rate remain fixed read-only constants.

demos.title: Fixed exponential decay over time
demos.learning_goal: Observe the magnitude and its negative instantaneous rate across the supplied time interval.
try_this: Move time from 0 toward 6 and observe that both curves decrease in magnitude.
Compare the magnitude curve with the rate curve and note that the rate remains negative.
Check the displayed values at t=0 and t=4 against 4, -1, 4/e, and -1/e.
